Subject: Post-demo SLO checklist & MAP — next steps

Hi Claire / Tom —

Thanks again for your time on the demo today. Quick written recap so the team has a single place to iterate on requirements and next actions. Overall we heard two top-level SLO asks from your side:

- Latency: P95 generation latency target of ~150ms for our primary short-form generation path (avg prompt length ~120 tokens).
- Concurrency/Throughput: target steady-state of 500 concurrent users (estimated 700-900 qps at peak), with burst capacity up to 1,500 qps for 10–15m windows.
- Streaming behavior: must support server-side streaming such that first-byte-to-client time (time-to-first-token) is <30ms for streaming flows; client-side chunking acceptable.
- Reliability: 99.9% successful responses during office hours (US PST), graceful fallback to smaller variant if our primary model exceeds latency SLOs.

Immediate asks from us:
1) Please confirm the targets above or flag incorrect items.
2) Share any sample prompt mixes or a small dataset (anonymized) we can use for the pre-pilot load tests.
3) Confirm decision criteria: is meeting 150ms P95 non-negotiable for the pilot, or do you prefer a graded acceptance (e.g., 150ms target with a 200ms acceptable ceiling during ramp)?

Next steps we propose:
- Internal prep: Marissa will spin up a staging run simulating your prompt mix and the concurrency profile (target start: this Wednesday 11 Mar).
- MAP: I will circulate a mutual action plan in the next 24 hours with dates for an initial load test, acceptance criteria and procurement touch points.

Attachments: I attached a first-pass SLO checklist and our suggested loadtest config for your review.

If this looks right I’ll lock the MAP and propose a brief 30-minute ops call to align on test harness and network egress (we may need a static IP allowlist).

Best,

Subject: Re: Post-demo SLO checklist & MAP — next steps

Hi Rishi —

Really helpful recap — thanks. A few clarifications from our side after the demo and a quick sync with our infra lead:

- Latency: 150ms P95 is the target for non-streamed completions (user expectations for page-load flows). For the real-time chat experience we need ~30–50ms to first-token (tight), and under 200ms P95 for the full response when prompts are short (<200 tokens).
- Concurrency: the 500 concurrent user figure is correct for steady-state; please plan tests at 750 qps for buffer. During marketing pushes we’ve seen bursts up to ~2,000 qps for 8–12 minutes — having a fallback model is ok for those windows.
- Streaming: we require chunked streaming with early partial output for UX. If your runtime can return first bytes in <30ms that’s ideal; if not, we need to see evidence of smoothing and UX-level retries.

Decision criteria: procurement will sign off for pilot if the initial load test meets 3 of 4: P95 latency <=200ms, time-to-first-token <50ms on streaming, error rate <0.5% under load, and documented autoscaling plan. Hitting 150ms P95 is preferred but not strictly deal-blocking for the pilot.

We’ll share an anonymized sample of 300 typical prompts by EOD. Also please share the MAP and an initial test window — we prefer the pilot start week of Mar 22.

Thanks,
Claire
SVP Product, Brightline Health
claire@brightlinehealth.com

Team — forwarding Claire's clarifications. Key items to prep for the staging run and MAP:

- Targets to validate in staging:
  * Streaming: time-to-first-token <30ms, P95 end-to-end <200ms for short prompts.
  * Non-streamed path: P95 <=150ms preferred, 200ms acceptable for pilot acceptance.
  * Error budget: <0.5% under simulated peak.
  * Concurrency profile: steady 500 concurrent, test at 750 qps and two burst tests at 1,500 and 2,000 qps for 10–15m windows.

- Proposed technical approach:
  * Use quantized 4-bit variant plus dynamic kernel selection for primary path; keep an unquantized variant for fallback.
  * Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (Claire to provide sample prompt set).
  * Streaming test needs client emulator that records time-to-first-byte and chunk intervals; Marissa, can you add BF-separated logging to capture first-token latency?

- Artifacts to produce:
  * Load test report with P50/P90/P95/P99 and error breakdowns.
  * Network diagram + static IP allowlist for Brightline.
  * Draft MAP (dates for test window, acceptance criteria) — attached (mutual-action-plan-draft.docx).

Marissa — can you schedule the first staging run on Wed 11 Mar (evening PST) and iterate on the loadtest-config.yaml I attached? Laura — please coordinate with infra to reserve a dedicated node pool and ensure metrics retention for 30 days (we need the logs for compliance ask).

I’ll own communications and the formal MAP to the customer. Let me know blockers.
